description: A pale, straight-grained, fine-textured Southeast Asian hardwood. Commonly sold as dowels, mouldings, picture frame stock, and toy and furniture parts.

hazards.summary: Occupational asthma from ramin dust was confirmed with skin tests and bronchial challenge in a Spanish study of obeche workers. The same patients reacted to ramin even if they had not worked with it, showing cross-reactivity between the two woods.
One worker developed an alveolitis-like illness from ramin dust; the drop in lung function was reproduced by an inhalation challenge in the laboratory.
HSE lists dermatitis from ramin and notes it may come from the bark. Two dermatology case reports describe skin sensitivity to ramin wood.
IARC classifies all wood dust as carcinogenic to humans, chiefly through cancers of the nose and sinuses. This applies to ramin dust as it does to any other wood.

related_species_note: Cross-reacts with obeche (Triplochiton scleroxylon) in sIgE inhibition studies (Hinojosa-1986).
image_prompt: Photorealistic studio photograph of a freshly planed ramin (Gonystylus bancanus) board, shot at a low three-quarter angle so the face grain fills most of the frame. Uniform pale straw to light creamy-yellow wood with no distinct heartwood or sapwood boundary. Straight to slightly interlocked grain, fine even texture with small evenly spread pores, and a modest natural luster. Soft diffused daylight from upper left, gentle falloff, neutral warm-grey seamless background, shallow depth of field with the near edge tack-sharp. No text, no logos, no hands, no tools, no finish or varnish, natural unfinished wood. Wide 1200x630 composition (1.91:1) with the board centered and margin on both sides for cropping.
image_alt: Planed board of ramin with uniform pale straw-colored wood and a fine, even, straight grain.
notes_internal: Beck-1982 and Bruynzeel-1987 have no abstracts; titles verified only. Whether they used patch testing is unknown, so the skin hazard stays at level 2 (HSE) and is typed skin_irritant (HSE says 'dermatitis' without stating allergic). Upgrade to skin_sensitizer level 1 if full text shows positive patch tests.
